KXCPI-26MAY-T0.4.reason: Tariff-driven goods inflation likely added upward pressure in May 2026, but shelter disinflation offsets some; MoM >0.4% probable but market may slightly overprice tail optimism.

KXCPI-26MAY-T0.5.reason: Exceeding 0.5% MoM requires both tariff and energy to deliver simultaneously; services ex-shelter trending down, making this threshold harder to clear.

KXCPI-26MAY-T0.6.reason: A 0.6%+ MoM print would be a significant surprise; possible only if energy spiked and tariff pass-through was faster than expected, slightly underpriced at 7c.

KXCPI-26MAY-T0.7.reason: A 0.7%+ MoM CPI in May 2026 would be historically elevated; fat tail risk from concurrent tariff + energy shock makes this slightly underpriced relative to 2c market.

KXCPI-26MAY-T0.8.reason: An 0.8%+ MoM print is an extreme outcome last seen during acute supply shocks; fair at 2c given the low base rate for such readings.
